observations.fact: For the three months ended March 28, 2026 Mobileye reported $558 million revenue versus $438 million in the comparable 2025 quarter; EyeQ SoC sales represented about 92% of revenue.
Four disclosed major-customer buckets each represented at least 10% of Q1 2026 revenue: 25%, 18%, 17%, and 15%, respectively.
Q1 2026 shipment-destination revenue included $130 million USA, $113 million China, $77 million Germany and $66 million South Korea, demonstrating geographic breadth but material country exposure.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Primary SEC filing shows Q1 revenue growth of roughly 27% year over year, while the revenue model remains highly concentrated in EyeQ SoCs and a small set of major customers.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Revenue is geographically distributed, but customer concentration and 92% EyeQ SoC revenue dependence create correlated execution risk if major OEM/Tier-1 programs or core SoC demand weaken.

risks.risk: Customer concentration is material: the four disclosed >=10% customer buckets sum to 75% of Q1 2026 revenue; Alpha should preserve this as concentration evidence rather than infer diversification from the broad OEM pipeline.
Core-product concentration remains material because EyeQ SoC sales represented approximately 92% of Q1 2026 revenue.

contradictions.statement: Strategic expansion into robotaxi and humanoid robotics broadens future optionality, but current reported revenue remains overwhelmingly EyeQ SoC-derived; optionality should not be treated as present diversification.

unknowns: The filing anonymizes major customers, so customer-specific dependency cannot be assigned without separate defensible lineage.
This artifact does not provide current market-price/valuation evidence and must not be used to manufacture a marketValuationOpportunity score.
confidence: high for filed revenue mix and concentration facts; moderate for factor interpretation
